sections.heading: Why the vowels matter
sections.body: French has more vowel sounds than Spanish or Italian, and several pairs change the meaning of a word: *dessus* (on top) and *dessous* (underneath) differ only in their last vowel. This lesson trains your ear and mouth on the pairs that matter most. Listen to each example several times.

sections.heading: [i], [y] and [u]: i, u, ou
sections.body:
- **[i]** — written **i** or **y**: *il*, *lit*, *ici*. Lips spread, like a smile.
- **[y]** — written **u**: *tu*, *rue*, *salut*. Keep your tongue where it is for [i], then round your lips tightly. English has no such sound.
- **[u]** — written **ou**: *vous*, *rouge*, *bonjour*. Like "oo" in "food", but tenser.

Compare these everyday pairs: *tu* /ty/ — *tout* /tu/ (all); *rue* /ʁy/ (street) — *roue* /ʁu/ (wheel); *dessus* — *dessous*.

sections.heading: [e] and [ɛ]: é and è
sections.body:
- **[e]** — a closed sound, lips spread: written **é**, **-er**, **-ez**, **et**: *café*, *parler*, *vous parlez*, *et*.
- **[ɛ]** — an open sound, mouth more open: written **è**, **ê**, **ai**, **e** before two consonants: *mère*, *fête*, *lait*, *elle*.

Compare: *et* /e/ (and) — *est* /ɛ/ (is). In everyday speech many people blur these, but you'll be understood best if you keep them apart.

sections.heading: [ø] and [œ]: eu
sections.body:
The spelling **eu** (or **œu**) has two closely related sounds, both made like [e] or [ɛ] but with rounded lips:

- **[ø]** — closed, at the end of a word or before a z sound: *deux*, *bleu*, *peu*, *heureuse*.
- **[œ]** — open, before a pronounced consonant: *heure*, *sœur*, *jeune*, *professeur*.

sections.heading: [o] and [ɔ]
sections.body:
- **[o]** — closed: written **au**, **eau**, **ô**, or **o** at the end of a word: *beau*, *eau*, *hôtel*, *vélo*.
- **[ɔ]** — open: **o** before a pronounced consonant: *porte*, *école*, *homme*.

examples: Tu habites dans quelle rue ?
Which street do you live on?
C'est tout.
That's all.
Le livre est dessus, le sac est dessous.
The book is on top, the bag is underneath.
Le café et le lait.
Coffee and milk.
Ma mère est à la fête.
My mother is at the party.
Elle est jeune et très belle.
She's young and very beautiful.
Ma sœur a deux vélos bleus.
My sister has two blue bikes.
Il est quelle heure ?
What time is it?
Un peu d'eau, s'il vous plaît.
A little water, please.
Il fait beau aujourd'hui.
The weather's nice today.
La roue du vélo est cassée.
The bike's wheel is broken.
Le professeur ouvre la porte de l'école.
The teacher opens the school door.
